thread:
lia_support: Heads-up — planning a late-night runtime pin + rolling rollout for inference runtime rti/v2.1 in us-east. Change window 23:00-02:00 UTC. Goal: pin hosted to v2.1 and perform staged canaries for Dedicated pools with fallback to v2.0 if issues.

keith_ops: +1. Are we doing a hard pin for Dedicated customers or a soft preference? I want the customer-facing comms to call out any SKU impact.

lia_support: Soft pin with explicit fallback. Dedicated will receive a config push to prefer v2.1 but we keep v2.0 as immediate fallback. I'll draft the status page snippet — need wording for SLA/latency expectations.

maria_product: Suggested copy: call out possible transient 5-10% latency variance during canary ramp. No expected data plane downtime. Mention that model outputs unchanged for >95% of calls based on internal evals.

sam_oncall: Deploy-bot will kick off canary at 23:15 UTC. Please be ready with immediate rollback steps. If any canary instance reports >2% 5xx or error rate spike, we pause and rollback.

deploy-bot: [automated] initiating canary: release=rti/v2.1, region=us-east, canary_nodes=2, start=23:15 UTC. Monitor channel #eng-oncall and /deploy logs.

ops: Observability runbook: key checks — 95th latency, 5xx rate, token cost delta, KV-cache hit rate. I’ll watch tracing and top-slow calls. If we see model hallucination regressions, escalate to Research.

keith_ops: For customers with Dedicated reserved capacity, ops will send a preflight note linking to the rollback opt-in. Also add a note about overnight maintenance windows for EU customers if ripple.

lia_support: Draft statuspage snippet below (please review). Will publish at 22:45 UTC as a scheduled maintenance message with expected window and contact links.

statuspage-bot: ````
Scheduled maintenance: Late-night runtime pin & staged rollout in US-East
Start: 23:00 UTC, Estimated end: 02:00 UTC
Impact: We expect no service interruption. During staged canaries (23:15–00:30) you may observe transient increases in latency for a small fraction of requests; error rates are not expected to exceed normal bounds. Dedicated customers: preference pin to rti/v2.1 will be applied; immediate fallback to rti/v2.0 is available if issues detected.
If you rely on strict latency SLOs, please contact support@redwood.com for an opt-out window during rollout.
````

maria_product: LGTM. Suggest adding: "If you see any change in output quality, report with an example and request an expedited rollback." Put link to eval form.

lia_support: Also drafting customer email/console message template — short, actionable. Putting below.

statuspage-bot: ````
Subject: Heads-up: Nighttime runtime pin and staged rollout (US-East)
Body: Hi — we will apply a preference pin to runtime rti/v2.1 and do a staged rollout between 23:00–02:00 UTC tonight. No service downtime expected. You may notice small, temporary latency increases during canaries. If you require an opt-out or have strict latency/quality constraints, reply to this email or open a ticket and we will coordinate an exception. Contact: support@redwood.com
````

sam_oncall: Rollback checklist (short):
1) Pause rollout via deploy-bot: `/deploy abort canary rti/v2.1 us-east`
2) Force route traffic to rti/v2.0: `rtctl set-preference region=us-east runtime=rti/v2.0`
3) Notify customers via statuspage update (short incident).
4) Collect traces and sample prompts, tag with `rollback-1769581234` and hand to Research.

keith_ops: Add a note for billing: no change to billing units for pinned runtime. Good to confirm.

lia_support: Final ask — @ops/@sam_oncall can one of you post the scheduled maintenance entry at 22:45 UTC and ping this thread when posted? I'll hold the customer email send until you confirm the statuspage live.

ops: Will post and ping. I’ll also attach the internal rollback runbook link in the scheduled message. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: [automated] canary started successfully. canary_id=cb-1769581234-01, monitor_link=https://deploys.internal/rti/v2.1/cb-1769581234-01

lia_support: Thanks — leaving the thread open for any last-minute changes. If we need to abort, call out here and tag @deploy-bot.
